column5: The report grows as you sell.
column6: F: Last time the report read the books. | M: This time we feed the books, and watch the Excel report grow.
M: GardenWorld again. Same company, same admin.

M: First, the Sales Register. One row for each sales invoice. | F: How many today? | M: Four invoices, totalling five hundred forty-one point oh two. | F: And where is the total? | M: Right under the last row. Remember that spot. It is the part that has to move.

column5: First sale: Joe Block buys mulch.
column6: F: Now a customer walks in. | M: Joe Block, at the till. We start a new POS order, and pick the customer and the organisation. Save. | F: Then the product? | M: A bag of mulch, quantity one. Save the line. | F: And then? | M: Complete. One click, and the ERP creates the shipment, the invoice, the stock move, and sixteen posting lines: revenue, receivable, cost of goods, and stock value. All in one signed step. | F: Nothing to retype? | M: Nothing. The ledger is already moving. The report only has to read it. | F: Why signed? | M: So every step can be checked afterwards.

M: Same again. A new order, same customer. | F: And two bags this time? | M: Two bags of mulch. Save the line, then Complete. | F: More lines? | M: Sixteen more posting lines, thirty-two in all. Each sale is its own signed step, checked as a chain. | F: Is the report changing yet? | M: Not yet. It only reads when we ask it to, and it reads the ledger as it stands at that moment.

M: And a third sale. Three bags. | F: Same steps? | M: Same steps. A new order, the same customer, the product, quantity three. Save the line, and Complete. | F: Anything different this time? | M: Only the numbers. Another sixteen posting lines, forty-eight in all. | F: Are the sales in the ledger now? | M: Yes. Three signed sales. But the report has not seen them yet. | F: So what happens to our four rows? | M: Let us run the register and see.

column5: Seven rows; the total moved down.
column6: F: Now run the register again. | M: Watch the rows. It had four lines. The report pushed the list down to make room, so now there are seven, one for each invoice. | F: And the total? | M: It moved down with them, and its range now covers rows six to thirteen. It went up by exactly eighteen: those three invoices.

F: Do the books still balance? | M: Trial balance, same session. Every sale posted its debits and credits together. Debit, forty-one thousand, two hundred eighty-three, seventy-eight. Credit, exactly the same. The difference is zero. | F: So the sales left the books clean. | M: Clean, and they are in the report.

F: Can we put it all back? | M: Clear the browser's local data, and GardenWorld reloads from its seed. Nothing to undo. | F: What gets cleared? | M: The local copy: the cache, the signer, and the operation log. Nothing is sent anywhere. | F: Why does that matter? | M: Because a demo or a test should never leave a mess. Enter data, report on it, wipe it, and start again. | F: And the register? | M: Four rows again. Five hundred forty-one point oh two. Exactly as before.
